description:
Set up sharing of pipelines without copying files into target repos. Needs ag-s99.1 first (until then the OIDC check rejects reusable workflows).

Decided with Matt on 2026-10-14:
- Split. The reporter actions (integrations/claude-code, integrations/claude-code-otlp) stay in the agbredo repo, because they change together with the server's report fields and OIDC checks. Pipelines go in a separate central repo (name to agree with Matt, e.g. xpmatteo/agbredo-agents), owned like an enterprise agent team would own them.
- Pipelines use the reporter as a remote composite action: uses: xpmatteo/agbredo/integrations/claude-code@<tag>. This needs release tags on agbredo, because every push to main deploys to Railway and pipelines must not follow main. Update integrations/claude-code/README.md, which today says to copy the directory.
- Each target repo keeps only a caller workflow: triggers, permissions (including id-token: write; a reusable workflow can only narrow permissions) and one jobs.<x>.uses: line pointing at the pipeline, plus secrets: inherit or explicit secrets.

How pipeline files reach the runner: inside a reusable workflow, actions/checkout and uses: ./... refer to the caller repo, not the central repo. So put each agent's scripts, prompts and settings in a composite action in the central repo and reference it with a full uses: owner/repo/path@ref; the runner downloads it and github.action_path points to its files (the reporter already finds report.py this way). The pipeline at @v1 calls its actions at @v1; bump both together. Alternative for the Claude parts: claude-code-action can install Claude Code plugins from a marketplace repo (check the current inputs, believed to be plugin_marketplaces and plugins).

Steps: create a tag on agbredo; create the central repo with one example pipeline (port examples/hello-agent or the "claude" scenario in .github/workflows/agbredo-example.yml); a caller workflow in a test repo; check a run reports to https://www.agbredo.com. Creating repos and tags is outward-facing: confirm with Matt first.

2026-10-14, Matt decided: the reporter is dropped (ag-s99.11), so there is nothing to publish but the telemetry action, already used remotely as xpmatteo/agbredo/integrations/claude-code-otlp. Central repo = xpmatteo/agbredo-pipelines (empty today). First pipeline = rpg-interpreter's .github/workflows/agent-instructions-audit.yml. The checks file (.github/agent-instructions-checks.md) and all scripts (scripts/agent-instructions-refs.sh, the inline gate/awk/jq steps) move to the central repo for cohesion; inside a reusable workflow they are not checked out, so ship them in a composite action in the central repo (github.action_path), per the original plan. The Sarca note stays only in rpg-interpreter's caller workflow (pass it as an input, e.g. extra prompt text). rpg-interpreter keeps a caller workflow: schedule + workflow_dispatch, permissions incl. id-token: write, one uses: xpmatteo/agbredo-pipelines/.github/workflows/agent-instructions-audit.yml@v1, secrets. Matt approved: push agbredo-pipelines' first main, tag agbredo v1 (pipelines use claude-code-otlp@v1, not @main), tag agbredo-pipelines v1.
